qe: In February 1943, Mahatma Gandhi initiated a historic fast while in prison. Against what structural issue was this hunger strike primarily directed?
qh: फरवरी 1943 में, महात्मा गांधी ने जेल में रहते हुए एक ऐतिहासिक उपवास शुरू किया था। यह भूख हड़ताल मुख्य रूप से किस संरचनात्मक मुद्दे के खिलाफ निर्देशित थी?
o: The institutional violence of the colonial State
The refusal of the Congress to adopt the two-nation theory
The implementation of separate electorates for minority communities
The continuous entry of British managing agencies into coastal shipping
e: Detailed Explanation: Gandhi started his fast in February 1943 as a powerful answer to the government's exhortation to condemn popular unrest. The fast was explicitly directed against the high-handed structural violence of the colonial State itself.

qe: What major constitutional development occurred within the Viceroy’s Executive Council as a direct result of public outrage during Gandhi's 1943 fast?
qh: गांधी के 1943 के उपवास के दौरान जन आक्रोश के सीधे परिणाम के रूप में वायसराय की कार्यकारी परिषद (Viceroy’s Executive Council) के भीतर कौन सा बड़ा संवैधानिक घटनाक्रम हुआ था?
o: Three Indian members of the Viceroy's executive council resigned in protest
The council was immediately dissolved and replaced by a constituent assembly
The Governor-General surrendered his absolute veto power to the Premier
The absolute unification of the executive council with the Muslim League front
e: Detailed Explanation: As protests, hartals, and strikes erupted at home and abroad during the fast, the moral pressure forced exactly three prominent members of the Viceroy’s Executive Council to resign from their seats in protest.

qe: Which of the following was NOT an administrative or political achievement of Mahatma Gandhi's 1943 prison fast?
qh: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा महात्मा गांधी के 1943 के जेल उपवास का प्रशासनिक या राजनीतिक परिणाम नहीं था?
o: The British government formally agreed to grant immediate dominion status to the Indian Union
Public morale across the country was significantly raised
Anti-British feeling among different sections of society was heightened
An important opportunity was provided for renewed nationalist political activity
e: Detailed Explanation: The fast successfully raised public morale, heightened anti-British sentiments, and exposed the government's high-handedness. However, it did not compel the British government to grant immediate dominion status.

qe: On which specific date did the All India Muslim League officially observe 'Pakistan Day' during the peak of the wartime political vacuum in 1943?
qh: 1943 में युद्धकालीन राजनीतिक शून्य के चरम के दौरान अखिल भारतीय मुस्लिम लीग ने आधिकारिक तौर पर किस विशिष्ट तिथि को 'पाकिस्तान दिवस' (Pakistan Day) मनाया था?
o: March 23, 1943
February 14, 1931
August 31, 1920
e: Detailed Explanation: While the mainstream national movement was grappling with leadership arrests and the post-fast scenario, the Muslim League officially observed Pakistan Day on March 23, 1943.

qe: The veteran Congress leader C. Riveragopalachari prepared a specialized scheme in 1944 to bridge the constitutional deadlock. What did this plan structurally represent?
qh: दिग्गज कांग्रेस नेता सी. राजगोपालाचारी ने 1944 में संवैधानिक गतिरोध को दूर करने के लिए एक विशेष योजना तैयार की थी। यह योजना संरचनात्मक रूप से किसे दर्शाती थी?
o: A tacit acceptance of the Muslim League’s demand for Pakistan to secure Congress-League cooperation
The complete, absolute validation of Lord Birkenhead's constitutional challenges
A legislative blueprint to permanently integrate the Kingdom of Nepal into British India
The mandatory conversion of all provincial legislative councils into non-elected bodies
e: Detailed Explanation: The CR Plan (1944) formulated a strategy for Congress-League cooperation. It was significant because it represented a tacit, realistic acceptance of the Muslim League's underlying demand for a separate Pakistan by a frontline Congress leader.

qe: Under the terms of the 1944 CR Plan, what baseline political obligation was demanded from the Muslim League in return for a post-war plebiscite?
qh: 1944 के सीआर प्लान (CR Plan) की शर्तों के तहत, युद्ध के बाद जनमत संग्रह के बदले मुस्लिम लीग से कौन सी बुनियादी राजनीतिक प्रतिबद्धता मांगी गई थी?
o: The Muslim League had to endorse the Congress demand for independence and cooperate in forming a provisional central government
The League had to completely dissolve its organizational infrastructure across all provinces
The mandatory rejection of separate communal electorates inside the central assembly
To provide extensive financial credit inputs to support the newly established national schools
e: Detailed Explanation: The CR Plan stipulated that the Muslim League must endorse the Congress demand for independence and actively cooperate with the Congress in establishing a provisional interim government at the center.

qe: According to the territorial arrangements of the 1944 CR Plan, which specific geographical zones were designated to undergo a popular plebiscite after the war?
qh: 1944 के सीआर प्लान के क्षेत्रीय समझौतों के अनुसार, युद्ध के बाद किन विशिष्ट भौगोलिक क्षेत्रों में जनमत संग्रह (plebiscite) कराया जाना तय किया गया था?
o: The Muslim majority areas in North-West and North-East India
The entire unified baseline territory of the Bengal and Bombay Presidencies
Only the princely states that refused to allotment 52 seats in the Council of States
The landlocked alluvial plains of Bihar and the Chhotanagpur tribal belt exclusively
e: Detailed Explanation: The CR Plan proposed that after the conclusion of World War II, the entire population residing within the Muslim-majority areas of North-West and North-East India would decide via a democratic plebiscite whether to separate.

qe: What structural condition was appended to the 1944 CR Plan layout regarding the activation of its constitutional terms?
qh: 1944 की सीआर योजना के खाके में उसकी संवैधानिक शर्तों के लागू होने के संबंध में कौन सी संरचनात्मक शर्त जोड़ी गई थी?
o: The terms would be operative only if England transferred full powers to India
The proposals were dependent on the unique financial validation of the Aligarh School
The terms required the immediate, absolute partition of the country before the war ended
The plan would function only within the non-votable items of the 1919 Act
e: Detailed Explanation: The CR Plan featured an essential safeguard for national integrity: all its terms and compromise clauses would become operational only if England transferred full, absolute sovereign powers to India.

qe: Why did Mohammad Ali Jinnah strongly object to the provisions of the 1944 CR Plan, leading to the failure of his discussions with Gandhi?
qh: मोहम्मद अली जिन्ना ने 1944 के सीआर प्लान के प्रावधानों पर कड़ा ऐतराज क्यों जताया, जिससे गांधी के साथ उनकी बातचीत विफल हो गई?
o: He wanted the Congress to accept the two-nation theory, opposed a common center, and wanted only Muslims to vote in the plebiscite
He demanded that the plebiscite be expanded to include all Hindu majority provinces
He vehemently objected to the creation of separate Muslim-majority units in Sindh
He sought to protect the executive veto powers of the central Governor-General permanently
e: Detailed Explanation: Jinnah rejected the CR Plan because he demanded that the Congress officially acknowledge the two-nation theory first. He also opposed a common central machinery for subjects like defence, and insisted that only the Muslim population of the targeted areas vote in the plebiscite, not the entire population.

qe: Which prominent group of nationalist leaders fiercely condemned the CR Plan, rejecting any compromise on the territorial integrity of the Indian Union?
qh: राष्ट्रवादी नेताओं के किस प्रमुख समूह ने भारतीय संघ की क्षेत्रीय अखंडता पर किसी भी समझौते को अस्वीकार करते हुए सीआर प्लान (CR Plan) की तीखी निंदा की थी?
o: Hindu leaders led by Vir Savarkar
The Congress Socialist Party led by Jayaprakash Narayan
The underground active cadres of the Forward Bloc
The radical ulema networks belonging to the Deoband school
e: Detailed Explanation: The proposals of the CR Plan faced stiff opposition from right-wing nationalist circles. Hindu leaders, spearheaded by Vir Savarkar, heavily condemned the plan for making concessions toward partition.

qe: The Desai-Liaqat Pact was formulated as a draft proposal to establish an interim government at the center. Which respective legislative positions did these two leaders hold at that time?
qh: केंद्र में एक अंतरिम सरकार स्थापित करने के लिए एक मसौदा प्रस्ताव के रूप में देसाई-लियाकत समझौते को तैयार किया गया था। उस समय इन दोनों नेताओं के पास कौन से विधायी पद थे?
o: Bhulabhai Desai was the leader of the Congress Party, and Liaqat Ali Khan was the deputy leader of the Muslim League in the Central Legislative Assembly
Desai was the Speaker of the Federal Assembly, and Liaqat was an Executive Councillor
Bhulabhai Desai was the Premier of Bombay, and Liaqat Khan was the Secretary of State
Both were non-official nominated elite members representing the zamindari interests of Bihar
e: Detailed Explanation: The pact was an informal negotiation inside the legislature. Bhulabhai Desai was the leader of the Congress Party in the Central Legislative Assembly, while Liaqat Ali Khan served as the deputy leader of the Muslim League in that same Assembly.

qe: What structural composition was proposed for the central legislature under the terms of the Desai-Liaqat Pact draft?
qh: देसाई-लियाकत समझौते (Desai-Liaqat Pact) की शर्तों के तहत केंद्रीय विधायिका के लिए किस संरचनात्मक संरचना का प्रस्ताव किया गया था?
o: An equal number of persons nominated by the Congress and the League, along with 20% reserved seats for minorities
An absolute official majority composed entirely of European administrative bureaucrats
Seats allocated strictly based on the military recruitment importance of Punjab and Bombay
A complete replacement of the legislative councils by the executive committee of the landholders
e: Detailed Explanation: The Desai-Liaqat draft proposed an interim central framework based on parity: it called for an equal number of nominees from both the Congress and the League in the legislature, supplemented by exactly 20% reserved seats for minority communities.

qe: Although no final settlement could be reached on the lines of the Desai-Liaqat Pact, what far-reaching political consequence did it produce for future negotiations?
qh: यद्यपि देसाई-लियाकत समझौते की तर्ज पर कोई अंतिम समझौता नहीं हो सका, फिर भी इसने भविष्य की वार्ताओं के लिए कौन सा दूरगामी राजनीतिक परिणाम पैदा किया?
o: It established a sort of parity between the Congress and the Muslim League
It caused the immediate legal dissolution of the All India Muslim League infrastructure
It forced the Congress Working Committee to completely abandon the goal of Purna Swaraj
It led to the total elimination of separate communal electorates from provincial councils
e: Detailed Explanation: Even though the pact failed to be implemented, the fact that a baseline structural 'parity' between the Congress and the Muslim League was formally proposed and accepted during discussions had deep, far-reaching consequences for later constitutional deadlocks.

qe: When the war in Europe terminated in May 1945, the British Conservative government led by Churchill felt keen to find an immediate solution to the Indian constitutional crisis. What primary domestic reason drove this eagerness?
qh: जब मई 1945 में यूरोप में युद्ध समाप्त हो गया, तो चर्चिल के नेतृत्व वाली ब्रिटिश कंजर्वेटिव सरकार ने भारतीय संवैधानिक संकट का तत्काल समाधान खोजने में गहरी उत्सुकता दिखाई। इस उत्सुकता के पीछे प्राथमिक घरेलू कारण क्या था?
o: The British general election was scheduled for mid-1945, and the Conservatives wanted to appear sincere in reaching a solution
The sudden, complete physical bankruptcy of the British Parliament exchequer lines in London
A direct legal order passed by the newly established international United Nations body
To provide massive financial subsidies to support the newly established swadeshi enterprises
e: Detailed Explanation: The Conservative cabinet faced domestic electoral constraints. With a British general election scheduled for mid-1945, Churchill's party wanted to demonstrate political sincerity in resolving the Indian deadlock to win voters.

qe: Viceroy Lord Wavell convened a high-prestige conference at Shimla in June 1945. What was the central structural objective of the proposals outlined in the Wavell Plan?
qh: वायसराय लॉर्ड वेवेल ने जून 1945 में शिमला में एक उच्च स्तरीय सम्मेलन बुलाया था। वेवेल योजना (Wavell Plan) में रेखांकित प्रस्तावों का मुख्य संरचनात्मक उद्देश्य क्या था?
o: To reconstruct the Governor-General’s Executive Council pending the preparation of a new constitution
The immediate and complete absolute dismantling of the Government of India Act 1935 framework
To organize a combined military operation to annex the northern frontier tribal areas permanently
The structural transfer of the central legislative assembly to the city of Allahabad limits
e: Detailed Explanation: The Wavell Plan was designed as an intermediate provisional arrangement. Its main goal was to completely reconstruct the Governor-General’s Executive Council while political forces prepared a new long-term constitution.

qe: Under the executive council reconstruction guidelines of the Wavell Plan, which two high positions were explicitly excluded from being Indianized?
qh: वेवेल योजना के कार्यकारी परिषद के पुनर्गठन दिशानिर्देशों के तहत, किन दो उच्च पदों को स्पष्ट रूप से भारतीयकरण (Indianized) से बाहर रखा गया था?
o: The Governor-General and the Commander-in-Chief
The Secretary of State and the Premier of Bengal
The Law Member and the Finance Executive Councillor
The Speaker of the Federal Assembly and the Chief Commissioner
e: Detailed Explanation: The Wavell Plan proposed that all members of the central Executive Council would be Indian nationals, with the explicit exception of two supreme imperial seats: the Governor-General and the Commander-in-Chief.

qe: What specific communal parity mechanism did the Wavell Plan introduce for nominations to the reconstructed Executive Council?
qh: वेवेल योजना ने पुनर्गठित कार्यकारी परिषद में नामांकन के लिए कौन सा विशिष्ट सांप्रदायिक समानता तंत्र (communal parity mechanism) पेश किया था?
o: Caste Hindus and Muslims were to have equal representation
Seats allocated strictly in a 3:1 ratio favoring the non-Brahmin intermediate groups
An absolute majority granted exclusively to the landless untouchable agricultural laborers
The mandatory reservation of 50% of the seats for the Anglo-Indian and Parsi delegates
e: Detailed Explanation: The Wavell Plan attempted to balance communal identities at the highest executive tier by stipulating that Caste Hindus and Muslims would enjoy strict equal representation within the council.

qe: Regarding accountability, how was the reconstructed Executive Council designed to function under the guidelines of the 1945 Wavell Plan?
qh: जवाबदेही के संबंध में, 1945 की वेवेल योजना के दिशानिर्देशों के तहत पुनर्गठित कार्यकारी परिषद को किस प्रकार कार्य करने के लिए डिज़ाइन किया गया था?
o: As an interim government functioning within the framework of the 1935 Act, meaning it was not responsible to the Central Assembly
As a fully responsible cabinet body that could be summarily voted out by a lower house majority
Subordinated entirely to the judicial verdicts of a three-judge panel of the High Court
Operating as a direct non-official advisory board answerable strictly to the village panchayats
e: Detailed Explanation: The reconstructed council under the Wavell Plan was structured to act as an interim government. However, it remained insulated from democratic accountability because it functioned within the old executive framework of the 1935 Act, meaning it was not responsible to the elected Central Assembly.

qe: Why did the All India Muslim League adopt an uncompromising stand during the Shimla Conference, demanding that all Muslim council members must be League nominees?
qh: अखिल भारतीय मुस्लिम लीग ने शिमला सम्मेलन के दौरान एक कड़ा और समझौता न करने वाला रुख क्यों अपनाया, और यह मांग की कि सभी मुस्लिम परिषद सदस्य लीग के नामांकित व्यक्ति होने चाहिए?
o: It feared that since other minorities shared Congress objectives, any other arrangement would reduce the League to a one-third minority
The leadership was legally forced to protect the regional premier seat of Khizr Hyat Khan
They aimed to secure absolute control over the non-votable 80% items of the central budget
They were financially backed by the British War Cabinet to veto the entry of any caste Hindus
e: Detailed Explanation: The League adopted a rigid position because it claimed to be the sole representative of Indian Muslims. They feared that since the socio-political aims of other minor groups (Sikhs, Depressed Classes, Christians) matched the Congress, allowing non-League Muslims into the council would effectively reduce the League to an uninfluential one-third minority.

qe: Viceroy Lord Wavell wanted to include which prominent non-League leader as the Muslim representative from Western Punjab, directly challenging Jinnah's claims?
qh: वायसराय लॉर्ड वेवेल जिन्ना के दावों को सीधे चुनौती देते हुए पश्चिमी पंजाब से मुस्लिम प्रतिनिधि के रूप में किस प्रमुख गैर-लीग नेता को शामिल करना चाहते थे?
o: Khizr Hyat Khan
Hakim Ajmal Khan
Hasan Imam
Hasrat Mohani
e: Detailed Explanation: Lord Wavell wanted to ensure regional representation by including Sir Khizr Hyat Khan, the non-League Unionist Premier of Punjab, as a Muslim representative in the council, which Jinnah flatly rejected.

qe: What specific political right or veto did the Muslim League claim during the executive council restructuring debates at Shimla?
qh: मुस्लिम लीग ने शिमला में कार्यकारी परिषद के पुनर्गठन की बहसों के दौरान किस विशिष्ट राजनीतिक अधिकार या वीटो का दावा किया था?
o: Decisions opposed to Muslims would require a two-thirds majority for approval inside the council
The absolute right to independently certify any bill rejected by the central legislature
An exclusive statutory power to select the Commander-in-Chief of the armed forces
The right to completely halt any land revenue collections across the eastern provinces
e: Detailed Explanation: To entrench its power, the Muslim League demanded a communal veto inside the Executive Council, asserting that any administrative decision opposed by the Muslim members would require a clear two-thirds majority to be approved.

qe: The Indian National Congress strongly rejected the Wavell Plan's communal framing. What primary objection did they log against the proposal?
qh: भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस ने वेवेल योजना के सांप्रदायिक ढांचे को कड़े रूप से खारिज कर दिया। उन्होंने प्रस्ताव के खिलाफ कौन सा मुख्य विरोध दर्ज कराया था?
o: They objected to it as an attempt to reduce the Congress to the status of a purely caste Hindu party and insisted on its right to include members of all communities
They fiercely opposed the provision that allowed free India to withdraw from the British Commonwealth
They demanded that the entire executive council must be composed strictly of wealthy urban zamindars
They completely rejected the right of women voters to hold franchise on the same basis as men
e: Detailed Explanation: The Congress took a secular stand and opposed the plan, arguing that it was a deliberate attempt to reduce the pan-Indian Congress to the narrow status of a purely caste Hindu faction. They insisted on their historical right to nominate national representatives from all communities, including Muslims.

qe: What major tactical blunder did Viceroy Lord Wavell commit that directly strengthened the Muslim League’s political veto and boosted Jinnah's standing before the 1945-46 elections?
qh: वायसराय लॉर्ड वेवेल ने कौन सी बड़ी रणनीतिक भूल की जिसने सीधे तौर पर मुस्लिम लीग के राजनीतिक वीटो को मजबूत किया और 1945-46 के चुनावों से पहले जिन्ना की स्थिति को बढ़ा दिया?
o: He unilaterally announced a complete breakdown of talks, effectively granting the League a virtual veto
He ordered the immediate rearrest of the entire Congress Working Committee panel inside Shimla
He passed an emergency ordinance completely nationalizing all swadeshi enterprise factories
He forcefully transferred the supervisory control over High Courts directly to the Muslim League
e: Detailed Explanation: Instead of bypassing the League's objections, Wavell abruptly closed the conference and announced a breakdown of talks. This tactical mistake granted the Muslim League a virtual veto over constitutional progress, heavily boosting Jinnah's prestige and position before the 1945–46 elections.

qe: In February 1946, the newly elected Attlee government decided to dispatch a high-powered Cabinet Mission to India. Who were the three British cabinet members who composed this body?
qh: फरवरी 1946 में, नवनिर्वाचित एटली सरकार ने भारत में एक उच्च-अधिकार प्राप्त कैबिनेट मिशन (Cabinet Mission) भेजने का निर्णय लिया। इस संस्था का गठन करने वाले तीन ब्रिटिश कैबिनेट सदस्य कौन थे?
o: Pethick Lawrence, Stafford Cripps, and A.V. Alexander
Winston Churchill, L.S. Amery, and Sir John Simon
Lord William Hunter, Sir Sidney Rowlatt, and Edwin Montagu
Lord Linlithgow, Lord Wavell, and Wedgewood Benn
e: Detailed Explanation: The Attlee government sent a high-level delegation in February 1946 consisting of three British Cabinet ministers: Lord Pethick Lawrence (Secretary of State for India and chairman), Sir Stafford Cripps (President of the Board of Trade), and A.V. Alexander (First Lord of the Admiralty).

qe: What was the explicit stated mandate of the 1946 Cabinet Mission when it was dispatched to the sub-continent by the British government?
qh: 1946 के कैबिनेट मिशन को जब ब्रिटिश सरकार द्वारा उपमहाद्वीप में भेजा गया था, तो उसका स्पष्ट घोषित शासनादेश (stated mandate) क्या था?
o: To find out ways and means for a negotiated, peaceful transfer of power to India
To forcefully implement the separate electorates schedule designed by the Communal Award
To launch a comprehensive scientific inquiry into the crisis of Indian agriculture fields
To mandate the absolute centralization of all provincial high courts under a single military bench
e: Detailed Explanation: Recognizing that direct governance was collapsing, the Attlee administration sent the Cabinet Mission with a clear, historic purpose: to negotiate and determine the ways and means for a peaceful transfer of power to Indian hands.

qe: By the end of World War II, a major structural shift had occurred inside the Indian Civil Service (ICS) that undermined British bureaucratic dominance. What was this shift?
qh: द्वितीय विश्व युद्ध के अंत तक, भारतीय सिविल सेवा (ICS) के भीतर एक बड़ा संरचनात्मक बदलाव आया था जिसने ब्रिटिश नौकरशाही के वर्चस्व को कमजोर कर दिया था। यह बदलाव क्या था?
o: A policy of Indianization and a paucity of European recruits had ended British domination, establishing a British-Indian parity as early as 1939
The complete administrative transfer of all recruitment powers directly to the local village panchayats
The legal passage of a decree that completely barred any European from entering the services
The mandatory financial payment of all bureaucratic salaries out of the Tilak Swaraj Fund savings
e: Detailed Explanation: The administrative grip of the Raj was broken from within. Due to a steady policy of Indianization and a lack of European recruits, British dominance over the elite Indian Civil Service (ICS) had dissipated, creating a structural British-Indian parity as early as 1939.

qe: Why did the British services and bureaucracy face an intense operational dilemma in the provinces during the post-war national scenario?
qh: युद्धोत्तर राष्ट्रीय परिदृश्य के दौरान प्रांतों में ब्रिटिश सेवाओं और नौकरशाही को एक तीव्र परिचालन दुविधा का सामना क्यों करना पड़ा था?
o: The constant mix of conciliation and repression, compounded by the prospect of radical Congress ministries coming to power
The central Legislative Assembly passed an ordinance completely abolishing the office of the district magistrate
The complete physical refusal of the agrarian peasants to utilize any imported currency notes
They were legally forced by the High Courts to undergo manual labor inside the local arsenal workshops
e: Detailed Explanation: The services faced a dilemma due to the conflicting colonial policy of alternating between conciliation and force. This confusion was deeply compounded by the political reality that the very Congress agitations they were suppressing were poised to form sovereign provincial ministries.

qe: What specific military and naval rebellions in the post-war phase raised severe fears that the armed forces were no longer reliable instruments to crush future mass movements?
qh: युद्धोत्तर चरण में किन विशिष्ट सैन्य और नौसैनिक विद्रोहों ने गंभीर आशंकाएँ पैदा कीं कि सशस्त्र बल अब भविष्य के जन आंदोलनों को कुचलने के लिए विश्वसनीय साधन नहीं रह गए हैं?
o: Demands of leniency for INA prisoners from within the Army and the revolt of the RIN ratings
The synchronized armed mutiny organized by the Chapekar secret samiti cells in Poona
The physical parameter attacks executed by the Bharat Naujawan Sabha against local arsenals
A mass walkout of all Indian pilots from the maritime transport shipping lines
e: Detailed Explanation: The imperial state recognized its coercive instruments were fracturing. Widespread demands within the Army for leniency toward Indian National Army (INA) prisoners, combined with the open mutiny of the Royal Indian Navy (RIN) ratings, shattered any illusions that the armed forces would remain loyal during another mass struggle.

qe: An analytical note by the historian B.R. Tomlinson describes that the British Cabinet and Viceroy Linlithgow viewed which factor as their ultimate 'trump card' against nationalist demands?
qh: इतिहासकार बी.आर. टॉमलिंसन का एक विश्लेषणात्मक नोट यह वर्णन करता है कि ब्रिटिश कैबिनेट और वायसराय लिनलिथगो ने राष्ट्रवादी मांगों के खिलाफ किस कारक को अपना अंतिम 'ट्रम्प कार्ड' (trump card) माना था?
o: The growing political rift and rivalry between the Congress and the Muslim League
The absolute economic consolidation of the non-votable items inside central budgets
The continuous legal expansion of the separate electorates to all intermediate castes
The direct financial contributions realized from the wealthy pro-British zamindars
e: Detailed Explanation: B.R. Tomlinson documented that the colonial machinery deliberately weaponized communal differences. Both the British Cabinet and Linlithgow treated the widening political rift and rivalry between the Congress and the Muslim League as their most useful weapon to stall nationalist demands.

qe: In a candid communication to his superiors in October 1946, Viceroy Lord Wavell recorded a grim assessment of British power. What did he state regarding their capacity to control events?
qh: अक्टूबर 1946 में अपने वरिष्ठों को भेजे गए एक स्पष्ट पत्र में, वायसराय लॉर्ड वेवेल ने ब्रिटिश सत्ता का एक गंभीर मूल्यांकन दर्ज किया था। घटनाओं को नियंत्रित करने की उनकी क्षमता के संबंध में उन्होंने क्या कहा था?
o: Our time in India is limited and our power to control events almost gone; we have only prestige and previous momentum to trade on
The administrative efficiency of the war-weary bureaucracy has completely stabilized across all provinces
The legal framework of the 1935 Act fully arms the Governor-General to suppress any future agitations easily
The armed forces remain absolute reliable instruments to execute an all-out repression of mass movements
e: Detailed Explanation: Confronting structural collapse, Lord Wavell wrote a private letter in October 1946 admitting the reality of British decline, noting that their time was limited, their control over events was almost completely gone, and they were merely trading on past prestige and momentum.

qe: A survey tracking vehicle maps a precise right-angled triangular course from central node O. It travels 48 km North, and then shifts orientation to drive 14 km East to reach storage point S. Find the direct straight-line distance from O to S.
qh: एक अनुसंधान वाहन केंद्रीय नोड O से एक सटीक समकोण त्रिकोणीय मार्ग का मानचित्रण करता है। यह 48 किमी उत्तर की ओर यात्रा करता है, और फिर पूर्व की ओर 14 किमी जाकर भंडारण बिंदु S पर पहुंचता है। O से S की सीधी रेखा की दूरी ज्ञात कीजिए।
o: 50 km
62 km
54 km
52 km
e:
Detailed Explanation: This spatial travel sets up a right-angled triangle with perpendicular legs measuring 48 km and 14 km. The straight-line distance represents the hypotenuse.
Applying the Pythagoras theorem: $\text{Distance} = \sqrt{48^2 + 14^2} = \sqrt{2304 + 196} = \sqrt{2500} = \mathbf{50\text{ km}}$.

qe: In an ecosystem productivity study tracking energy metrics, if the Net Primary Productivity (NPP) of a forest biome is measured at 36,000 units and the energy spent during metabolic plant respiration (R) is 24,000 units, calculate the Gross Primary Productivity (GPP).
qh: ऊर्जा मानकों पर नज़र रखने वाले एक पारितंत्र उत्पादकता अध्ययन में, यदि एक वन बायोम की शुद्ध प्राथमिक उत्पादकता (NPP) 36,000 इकाइयाँ मापी जाती है और पौधों के श्वसन (R) के दौरान खर्च की गई ऊर्जा 24,000 इकाइयाँ है, तो सकल प्राथमिक उत्पादकता (GPP) की गणना करें।
o: 60,000 units
12,000 units
48,000 units
50,000 units
e:
Detailed Explanation: Utilizing the ecological energy relationship formula: $NPP = GPP - R$, we isolate Gross Primary Productivity: $GPP = NPP + R$.
Substituting the values: $GPP = 36,000 + 24,000 = \mathbf{60,000\text{ units}}$.

qe: Why did the British administration find it structurally impossible to deploy an 'all-out repression' against the post-war upsurge of the nationalist mass movement?
qh: ब्रिटिश प्रशासन को राष्ट्रवादी जन आंदोलन के युद्धोत्तर उभार के खिलाफ 'पूर्ण दमन' (all-out repression) लागू करना संरचनात्मक रूप से असंभव क्यों लगा?
o: The necessary numbers of British forces and efficient administrative officials were simply not available to execute purely official rule
The Central Legislative Assembly had passed a resolution completely defunding the provincial police budgets
The International Court of Justice had legally threatened the British Crown with severe financial trade penalties
The conservative loyalist groups had voluntarily integrated their networks with the Congress left wing
e: Detailed Explanation: Direct military rule was no longer a viable option. The only alternative to a negotiated settlement was an entirely official, repressive rule, which was structurally impossible because the depleted, war-weary bureaucracy lacked the required numbers of efficient personnel.

qe: The Government of India Act of 1858 introduced a profound constitutional shift in the administrative structure of the sub-continent by executing which measure?
qh: भारत सरकार अधिनियम 1858 ने कौन सा उपाय करके उपमहाद्वीप के प्रशासनिक ढांचे में एक गहरा संवैधानिक बदलाव पेश किया था?
o: Transferring the power to govern from the East India Company directly to the British Crown, to be wielded through a Secretary of State
Establishing complete provincial autonomy under popular native ministerial portfolios with zero central control
Abolishing the office of the Viceroy and creating the separate Federal Court structure at Allahabad
Scrapping the supervisory control of the British Parliament over Indian revenues permanently
e: Detailed Explanation: Following the 1857 Revolt, the Act of 1858 dissolved the East India Company. It transferred the sovereign power to govern India directly to the British Crown, to be exercised through a cabinet post, the Secretary of State for India, who was assisted by a 15-member council and made directly answerable to the British Parliament.

qe: What macro-level transformation occurred to India's dynamic share of global manufacturing exports across the centuries of British colonial rule?
qh: ब्रिटिश औपनिवेशिक शासन के सदियों के दौरान वैश्विक विनिर्माण निर्यात (world manufacturing exports) में भारत की गतिशील हिस्सेदारी में बड़े पैमाने पर क्या परिवर्तन आया?
o: It dramatically fell from 27 per cent down to a mere 2 per cent
It increased steadily from 2 per cent up to an optimized 27 per cent
It remained perfectly constant at a balanced 10 per cent layout
It dropped to zero instantly within the first decade of the Charter Act of 1813
e: Detailed Explanation: As highlighted by modern economic historians, the systemic deindustrialization and forced commercialization under British rule caused India's share of world manufacturing exports to crash from a dominant 27 per cent down to a mere 2 per cent by the end of the colonial era.

qe: The judicial framework of the Cornwallis Code of 1793 established a major milestone in modern Indian administrative history by firmly introducing which concept?
qh: 1793 के 'कॉर्नवॉलिस कोड' ने किस प्रमुख अवधारणा को दृढ़ता से पेश करके आधुनिक भारतीय प्रशासनिक इतिहास में एक बुनियादी मील का पत्थर स्थापित किया?
o: The principle of the sovereignty of law and the separation of revenue and justice administration
The absolute legal immunity of all colonial government officials from civil court oversight
The mandatory use of English instead of vernacular languages across all local lower subdivisions
The total structural centralization of all judicial functions under the district Collector
e: Detailed Explanation: The Cornwallis Code of 1793 was a landmark because it established the sovereignty of law and the separation of powers. It separated revenue administration from justice, divested the Collector of judicial duties, and made government officials answerable to civil courts for official actions.

qe: In 1860, a judicial modification regulated the privileges of European subjects in India. What restriction did it place on judges of Indian origin regarding criminal cases?
qh: 1860 में, एक न्यायिक संशोधन ने भारत में यूरोपीय विषयों के विशेषाधिकारों को विनियमित किया। इसने आपराधिक मामलों के संबंध में भारतीय मूल के न्यायाधीशों पर कौन सा प्रतिबंध लगाया था?
o: No judge of an Indian origin could legally try a European subject in a criminal case
Indian judges were stripped of any original jurisdiction over civil property disputes involving Europeans
They were legally forced to refer all native criminal files directly to the local Munsiff benches
Indian judges were required to pass all their sentences strictly in classical European ciphers
e: Detailed Explanation: Reflecting the deeply rooted racial discrimination within the colonial legal architecture, a judicial regulation enacted in 1860 specified that while European subjects were brought under court jurisdiction, no judge of Indian origin possessed the legal authority to try a European subject in a criminal case.

qe: Under the central executive guidelines of the Government of India Act, 1919, what specific bicameral houses had replaced the old unicameral Imperial Legislative Council?
qh: भारत सरकार अधिनियम 1919 के केंद्रीय कार्यकारी दिशानिर्देशों के तहत, किन विशिष्ट द्विसदनीय सदनों ने पुरानी एकसदनीय इंपीरियल लेजिस्लेटिव काउंसिल का स्थान लिया था?
o: The Central Legislative Assembly (lower house) and the Council of State (upper house)
The House of Commons and the House of Lords structural branches
The British Indian Association and the All India Kisan Sabha chambers
The Sadar Diwani Adalat and the Sadar Nizamat legislative divisions
e: Detailed Explanation: The 1919 Act introduced a bicameral central legislature consisting of a lower house named the Central Legislative Assembly and an upper house named the Council of State, introducing the initial structural principle of a double-chamber parliament.

qe: The Royal Commission on Decentralization (1908) made a critical recommendation regarding the financial and administrative responsibilities of urban municipalities. What role did it suggest they should play in primary education?
qh: रॉयल कमीशन ऑन विकेंद्रीकरण (1908) ने शहरी नगर पालिकाओं की वित्तीय and प्रशासनिक जिम्मेदारियों के संबंध में एक महत्वपूर्ण सिफारिश की थी। इसने प्राथमिक शिक्षा में उनकी क्या भूमिका सुझाया था?
o: The municipalities might explicitly undertake the responsibility for primary education and, if willing, for middle vernacular schools
They should be completely barred from funding or managing any primary-level educational facilities locally
They were legally forced to route 100% of their primary school tax revenues directly to the Dayal Singh Trust in Lahore
The Commission suggested that municipalities should manage only high-cost advanced technical engineering universities
e: Detailed Explanation: To optimize local governance, the 1908 Decentralization Commission recommended that urban municipalities should explicitly take over the responsibility for funding and administering primary education and, if willing, middle vernacular schools, while being relieved of secondary education burdens.

qe: What retrogressive evaluation did the Simon Commission outline in its May 1930 report regarding the efficiency and financial management of local self-governing bodies since 1919?
qh: साइमन कमीशन ने मई 1930 की अपनी रिपोर्ट में 1919 के बाद से स्थानीय स्वशासी निकायों के कुशल और वित्तीय प्रबंधन के संबंध में कौन सा प्रतिगामी (retrogressive) मूल्यांकन प्रस्तुत किया था?
o: It claimed that the management of finances had deteriorated, and suggested the retrograde step of increasing provincial bureaucratic control over local bodies
It celebrated the village panchayats for successfully achieving absolute financial independence across all provinces
It demanded that 100% of local tax revenues must be channeled directly to support the All India Kisan Sabha
The Commission recommended the complete permanent legal abolition of the office of the district magistrate
e: Detailed Explanation: The Simon Commission (May 1930) noted that the financial management of local bodies had deteriorated since the introduction of the 1919 reforms, pointing out a lack of progress in village panchayats. Instead of expanding democracy, it recommended a retrograde step: increasing tight provincial bureaucratic control over these local bodies in the name of efficiency.
